title: Power Pages - Simply Explained
description:
Small businesses and IT teams need customer portals, partner hubs and self-service sites but rarely have web developers to build them. This episode explains Microsoft Power Pages: how it connects to Dataverse, how the Design Studio and Copilot speed up building, how security and licensing work, and where single-page apps and AI agents take the platform next.
In this episode
00:00 – What Power Pages is01:57 – From Power Apps portals to Power Pages03:05 – Dataverse: the engine behind the site04:58 – Building with the Design Studio and Copilot06:55 – Security: who sees what09:28 – Licensing and costs11:01 – Real-world use cases13:09 – What's next: SPAs, server logic and AI agents
Key takeaways
Power Pages is Microsoft's low-code platform for secure, external-facing websites that read and write live business data in Dataverse, unlike marketing sites built with WordPress or Squarespace.Sites are private by default and protected by a web application firewall, CDN, multiple identity providers, table and page permissions, web roles and the Deep Scan security tool.Standalone per-site licensing, a 30-day trial and new capabilities such as single-page applications, server logic and AI agents make it a full web application platform.
Worth quoting
“Think of it as a storefront for your business data. You have a back office full of customer records, orders, and service cases. Powerpages is the front door that lets your customers walk in and interact with that data.” – Mirko Peters (00:49)
“A WordPress site shows static content, but a Powerpages site shows live data from your business systems.” – Mirko Peters (01:38)
